input:
The performance of a natural-draft cooling tower at a chemical site was logged over the course of one summer month. During the logged month, the mean wet-bulb temperature was 27 °C, while the approach was 6 K and the range was 5 K. A natural-draft tower is essentially driven by the density difference that the range produces, so the logged approach of 6 K at a wet-bulb temperature of 27 °C effectively represents the performance that the tower was able to deliver under summer air conditions.

It is important to note, however, that the logged values describe only the logged month itself. Performance outside the logged month — in particular at the much lower wet-bulb temperatures encountered in winter — was not measured, and the summer approach cannot simply be transferred to winter operation, where both the wet-bulb temperature and the air density are different. In a similar way, the range of 5 K is also a summer figure, recorded at the summer heat load. The approach is the margin between the leaving water temperature and the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air, and it is generally the first term to move when the season changes, because colder and drier winter air lowers the wet-bulb temperature while the tower structure, the fill, and the water loading all remain exactly as built. Overall, no winter approach, range, or capacity figure is available from the logging exercise, and none has been inferred from the summer record.
target:
Performance of a natural-draft tower at a chemical site was logged over one summer month. The mean wet-bulb temperature over the logged month was 27 °C. The approach over the same month was 6 K and the range was 5 K. A natural-draft tower is driven by the density difference the range produces, and the logged approach of 6 K at a wet-bulb temperature of 27 °C is the performance the tower delivered under summer air conditions.

The logged values describe the logged month. Performance outside the logged month, in particular at winter wet-bulb temperatures, was not measured, and the summer approach does not transfer to winter operation, where the wet-bulb temperature and the air density both differ. The range of 5 K is likewise a summer figure, recorded at the summer heat load. No winter approach, range, or capacity figure is available from the logging, and none is inferred from the summer record.

The approach is the margin between the leaving water and the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air, and it is the term in the record that a change of season moves first: colder and drier air lowers the wet-bulb temperature, while the tower structure, the fill, and the water loading stay as built. The range is set by the heat load and the water rate rather than by the air, and a range held at the summer value under a winter load is a statement about the process, not about the tower. The record therefore supports a comparison of towers, or of one tower against its own earlier summer record, on the same seasonal basis; a cross-season comparison drawn from the record alone mixes a measured summer state with an unmeasured winter one, and the logging gives no basis for separating the two.
